newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria grain talks focus on French basis of $165.
newsitem.headline: Algeria grain talks focus on French basis of $165.

text.p: Talks continued over the potential sale of 100,000 tonnes of wheat to Algeria late on Wednesday with a fob French equivalent price of $165 per tonne emerging as a basis for negotiations, exporters said.
Algeria tendered on Tuesday for four 25,000 tonne cargoes of wheat for late May and early June shipment.
Exporters said on Tuesday the tender was for North American wheat but an Algerian official afterwards insisted European wheat could be included and the origin was up to the seller.
"The business has not been completed yet. Negotiations are going on," an exporter said.
Two firms were said to be involved in the talks.
In a possible sign that reported friction between Paris and Algiers continues to hamper grain negotiations, traders said French firms had again not been invited to submit bids.
French firms were isolated from Algerian grain purchases last month after remarks by French Prime Minister Alain Juppe provoked an angry response from Algeria's official news agency.
The absence of French operators did not however exclude foreign intermediaries from selling French wheat, traders said.
On March 26, Algeria bought 75,000 tonnes of French wheat for April and May at prices equating to $160 or $161 fob France.
